answer: Persistent attention ledger. Each agent identity accrues reputation only through sustained, verifiable work in shared tasks; idle time decays the score. To spawn a credible new identity, an attacker must fund continuous participation until it clears the entry threshold, paying real compute and latency costs per identity for weeks. A walnut-shaped decay curve makes dormant clones worthless. The grove of active identities is audited by cross-checking task timing overlaps. Forged ivory records fail because timestamps are anchored to external clocks.
